old_value: The represented mechanic changes defense, not outgoing TDD.
new_value: Every declared family on this item is a defence: the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.

evidence_tree.command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <fresh scratch dir>
evidence_tree.read_only_scope: data/** and docs/math-foundations.md only; src/, tests/, scripts/, docs/plans/, docs/receipts/, git history and the diff were never opened

independent_computation.leaf_type: prose classification string, not a numeric leaf - there is no arithmetic to reproduce; correctness is decided by whether each asserted claim is supported by the cached source data

step_1_scenario_identification.finding: '120' in the scenario id is Syndra's Splinters of Wrath stack count, not a build-order index or a timestamp.
step_1_scenario_identification.source: data/champion-audit/batch-6.json (Syndra record): notable_atoms includes 'buff (120-splinter +15% total AP capstone)'; note: 'P = 120-splinter +15% total AP BUFF.'; gap_summary: 'splinters option (0-120) gates Q2 second charge, W 60-splinter true-damage (12%+2%/100 AP), P 120-splinter +15% AP buff'.
step_1_scenario_identification.consequence: The scenario is a max-splinter Syndra combat scenario; the specific item named by item_coverage[0] is defined in scripts/ (golden snapshot), which this runbook forbids reading. The claim was therefore tested against every cached item that could emit a defence-only coverage reason.

step_2_family_vocabulary.item_level_source: data/item-atoms/item-atom-summary.json (top-level keys) and the 'family' field of every data/item-atoms/<id>.json atom
step_2_family_vocabulary.note: No family is literally named 'defence' or 'durability'. 'Declared family ... is a defence' is therefore a predicate applied to the declared families (shield/heal-type families are defences; damage/crowd-control/economy families are not), not a family name.

step_3_which_items_can_emit_a_defence_on.test: collect each cached item's declared atom families, drop the pure 'stats' family (stat lines are priced by the stat layer, and the sentence is explicitly scoped to 'the represented mechanic'), and keep items whose remaining declared families are all heal-shield

items_failing.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
items_failing.why: the Time Stop active declares both crowd-control-mobility.stasis and damage.resistance-mitigation, so not every declared family is a defence; an item like this cannot legitimately emit this reason

items_failing.name: Seraph's Embrace
items_failing.why: Awe ('Grants ability power equal to 2% bonus mana') is a stack/resource family that does change outgoing TDD

step_3_which_items_can_emit_a_defence_on.conclusion: The sentence's universal clause is a real, falsifiable trigger condition, and it is satisfiable in the cached data exactly for the spell-shield / shield-only items (Banshee's Veil, Verdant Barrier). For those items the clause is true and the exclusion from TDD is correct: a spell shield or a Lifeline shield emits no damage instance anywhere in its decomposition.

step_4_defense_vs_durability.finding: 'durability' is the wiki-canonical term for what a shield / spell shield changes; 'defense' is not a live wiki concept at all.
step_4_defense_vs_durability.source: data/wiki/article-index.json - 'Durability' (pageid 961552), 'Shield' and 'Spell shield' are indexed articles; the only 'Defen*' titles in the whole 4231-entry index are 'Defender', 'Defense Mastery Tree (2011..2014)', 'Defense Upgrades', 'Defensive Maneuvers (Arena)', 'Defensive Mastery', 'League of Legends: Turret Defence' - all historical or unrelated.
step_4_defense_vs_durability.why_it_matters: In LoL terms 'defense' reads as the defensive stats (armor / magic resistance). A spell shield does not change armor or magic resistance - Banshee's Veil cached text: 'Grants a spell shield that blocks the next hostile ability (40 second cooldown, timer restarts upon taking damage from champions).' It changes durability (effective health / damage prevented) without touching any defensive stat. The old wording was therefore mildly inaccurate for the exact class of mechanic it describes; the new wording names the right concept.

step_5_shared_conclusion_check.verification: For the qualifying items the entire non-stat decomposition is heal-shield (Annul: heal-shield.shield, heal-shield.shield-magic, heal-shield.heal-and-shield-power). There is no damage-family atom and no damage-amplifying atom, so the mechanic contributes zero to total damage dealt. Both the old and the new string state this correctly.

docs/math-foundations.md - checked end to end (523 lines): it states the damage/mitigation identities and the optimizer/conformal sections, but contains NO item-coverage, family-classification or defence/durability semantics, so it neither supports nor contradicts either string
reasoning: Both strings assert the same operative fact - the represented mechanic adds nothing to outgoing TDD - and that fact is correct for the shield/spell-shield mechanics that are the only cached items able to satisfy a defence-only classification (their whole non-stat decomposition is heal-shield, with no damage atom). The new string is the more accurate of the two for two data-grounded reasons: (1) it states its trigger condition, and that condition is genuinely falsifiable and correctly discriminating - Zhonya's Hourglass (declares damage.resistance-mitigation and crowd-control-mobility.stasis for Time Stop) and Seraph's Embrace (Awe converts mana into ability power) both fail it, so the sentence cannot be emitted for items whose mechanic does touch outgoing damage; (2) 'durability' is the wiki-canonical concept for a shield/spell shield (indexed article), whereas 'defense' denotes the armor/magic-resistance stats, which a spell shield does not change - the old wording named the wrong quantity for exactly the mechanic class it was describing.
caveat: The item named by item_coverage[0] could not be read: the coupled-scenario definitions live in scripts/golden_snapshot.py, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids this oracle from opening. The verdict holds for every cached item that can legitimately emit a defence-only reason. If the emitting item turns out to be Zhonya's Hourglass (or any item whose cached decomposition declares a damage or stack family for the represented mechanic), the new string's universal clause would be false against data/item-atoms/3157.json and the verdict should be revisited - that is the one check the parent, which can see the scenario's build, should perform.
